preamble: The shift from the voiceless uvular stop [q] to the voiceless velar stop [k] is a process of fronting. This change is frequently observed in languages losing the uvular-velar contrast, often driven by articulatory simplification or the influence of front vowels. Ecuadorian Kichwa (Quechua II-B) merged Proto-Quechuan *q with *k (*isqun > iskun 'nine').

examples.note: Yucatecan (Yucatec Maya, Lacandon, Itza') and Cholan-Tseltalan languages completely merged Proto-Mayan uvular *q with velar *k. This is one of the shared innovations distinguishing these branches from the more conservative K'ichean-Mamean and some Q'anjob'alan languages, which retain the uvular /q/ phoneme to the present day.

The ejective counterpart *q' also merged with k', so both plain and ejective uvulars were fronted to velars. This systematic pairing confirms the change was a phonological merger rather than sporadic substitution.
In some rural and peripheral Arabic dialects, the historical uvular /q/ has fronted to velar [k].
Systematic fronting where historical uvular series became velars, often as part of a chain shift.
Southern Quechua keeps a uvular (Cuzco isqun, Ayacucho isχun).
Kichwa does not distinguish Proto-Quechuan *k and *q; likewise killa means both 'moon' (Southern killa) and 'lazy' (Southern qilla [qeʎa]).
Root-final *q became a velar geminate in Fula; Sereer keeps the uvular (ceq).
Pozdniakov: the postvelar (uvular) consonants disappeared in Fula by merging with the velars in all positions; he counts 7 cases of Sereer -q ~ Fula -kk and none of Sereer -q ~ Fula -k.
